correctness.rationale: Exact 3D cube section area follows from coarea and a uniform-sum triangular-tail computation; polygon count follows from the face criterion. The unique maximizing normals are given by Ball's sharp slicing theorem. A local normalized coordinate chart has Jacobian 1/sqrt(2), uniform linear deficit g and a radial O(epsilon^2) boundary approximation, which yields the stated O(epsilon^3) probability errors. Exact sector integrations give the constants. A separately constructed cube-edge polygon verifier confirms area and face count in 1,958 cases, and separate finite-epsilon Haar quadratures approach the analytic constants. These numerical checks are not relied on as proofs.

value.rationale: The classical cube slicing inequality and its stability theory motivate measuring the angular mass of near-equality orientations. This new exact quadratic near-maximum probability and distinct conditioned quadrilateral/hexagon mechanisms quantify that mass and supply a full local angular limiting region. The result is a meaningful geometric-probability law rather than a restatement of the maximum or unconditional hexagon proportions.
